<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="transcriber" />{{RunningHeader|answer|231|ant}}</noinclude>f., answer, = Icel. ''andsvar'', ''annsvar'', neut., answer, response, decision, = Sw. Dan. ''ansvar'', responsibility, formerly answer), < ''and-'', against, in reply, + *''swaru'', f. (= Icel. ''svar'', usually in pl. ''svör'', neut., answer, = Sw. Dan. ''svar'', answer), < *''swaran'' (only in weak present ''swerian''), pret. ''swōr'', swear, = Icel. ''svara'', answer, respond, = Sw. ''svara'' = Dan. ''svare'', answer, respond, = Goth. ''swaran'', swear, prob. orig. ‘affirm, assert,’ with the subsequent implication, lost in the verb except in Scand., of ‘assert in reply’: see ''and-'', ''an-''<sup>2</sup>, and ''swear''. Hence ''answer'', ''v.''] '''1.''' A reply, response, or rejoinder, spoken or written, to a question (expressed or implied), request, appeal, prayer, call, petition, demand, challenge, objection, argument, address, letter, or to anything said or written.
{{smaller block|A soft ''answer'' turneth away wrath. {{right|Prov. xv. 1.}}}}
{{smaller block|I called him, but he gave me no ''answer''. {{right|Cant. v. 6.}}}}
{{smaller block|Bacon returned a shuffling ''answer'' to the Earl’s question. {{right|''Macaulay'', Lord Bacon.}}}}
In particular—(''a'') A reply to a charge or an accusation; a statement made in defense or justification of one’s self, {{smaller|with regard to a charge or an accusation; a defense; specifically, in ''law'', a pleading on the part of the defendant, responding to the plaintiff’s claim on questions of fact: correlative to ''demurrer'', which raises only questions of law. The word as used in equity nearly, and as used in recent codes of procedure closely, corresponds to the common-law ''plea''. (''b'') The solution of a problem; the result of a mathematical operation; a statement made in response to a question set for examination: implying correctness, unless qualified.}}
'''2.''' A reply or response in act; an act or motion in return or in consequence, either as a mere result due to obedience, consent, or sympathy, or as a hostile procedure in retaliation or reprisal.
{{smaller block|<poem>
If your father’s highness
Do not . . . . . . . . .
Sweeten the bitter mock you sent his majesty,
He’ll call you to so hot an ''answer'' of it,
That caves and womby vaultages of France
Shall chide your trespass, and return your mock
In second accent of his ordnance.
</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', Hen. V., ii. 4.}}}}
{{smaller block|<poem>
And so extort from us that
Which we have done, whose ''answer'' would be death
Drawn on with torture.
</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', Cymbeline, iv. 4.}}}}
{{smaller|Specifically —(''a'') In ''fencing'', the return hit.}}
{{smaller block|I had a pass with him, rapier, scabbard, and all, . . . and on the ''answer'', he pays you as surely as your feet hit the ground.
{{right|''Shak.'', T. N., iii. 4.}}}}
{{smaller|(''b'') In ''fugue-music'', the enunciation of the subject or theme by the second voice.}}

Often abbreviated to ''ans.'' and ''a.''
{{smaller|='''Syn.''' Reply, rejoinder, replication, response, retort, defense.}}

'''answer''' (ȧn′sėr), ''v.''   [Early mod. E. also ''answeare'', ''aunswer'', < ME. ''answeren'', ''answaren'', ''andsweren'', ''andswaren'', ''onsweren'', ''onswaren'', ''ondsweren'', ''ondswaren'', < AS. ''andswarian'', ''andswerian'', ''ondswarian'', ondswerian (pret. ''andswarode'') = OFries. ''ondswera'', ''onswera'', ''onsera'' = Icel. ''andsvara'', ''annsvara'', mod. ''anza'' = Sw. ''ansvara'' = Dan. ''ansvare'', answer, account for; from the noun.]   '''I.''' ''intrans.'' '''1.''' To make answer; speak or write in reply to a question (expressed or implied), request, appeal, petition, prayer, call, demand, challenge, address, argument, letter, or anything said or written; reply; respond: used with ''to'', or absolutely.
{{smaller block|Is thy news good, or bad? ''Answer to'' that.
{{right|''Shak.'', R. and J., ii. 5.}}}}
{{smaller block|<poem>Lives he?
Wilt thou not ''answer'', man?</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', A. and C., iv. 4.}}}}
{{smaller block|In particular—(''a'') To reply to a charge or an accusation; make a statement in defense or justification of one’s self, with regard to a charge or an accusation; specifically, in ''law'', to interpose a pleading responsive to plaintiff’s allegations of fact: sometimes used to include also the interposing of a demurrer: formerly sometimes with ''with''.}}
{{smaller block|Well hast thou ''answered with'' him, Radogan.
{{right|''Greene.''}}}}
{{smaller block|(''b'') To give a solution of a problem; find the result; give an answer, as to a question set for examination: as, he ''answered'' correctly in most instances.}}
'''2.''' To reply or respond in act; act or move in response; do something in return for or in consequence of some speech, act, or movement from another source.
{{smaller block|<poem>Now play him me, Patroclus,
Arming to ''answer'' in a night alarm.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', T. and C., i. 3.}}}}
{{smaller block|<poem>''Oct.'' Mark Antony, shall we give sign of battle?
''Ant.'' No, Cæsar, we will ''answer'' on their charge.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', J. C., v. 1.}}}}
{{smaller block|Those who till a spot of earth scarcely longer than is wanted for a grave, have deserved that the sun should shine upon its sod till violets ''answer''.
{{right|''Marg. Fuller'', Woman in 19th Cent., p. 17.}}}}
{{smaller block|Do the strings ''answer'' to thy noble hand? {{right|''Dryden''.}}}}
'''3.''' To speak in behalf of another; declare one’s self responsible or accountable, or give assurance or guaranty, for another; be responsible or accountable: used with ''for'', rarely absolutely: as, I will ''answer for'' his safety; I am satisfied, but I cannot ''answer for'' my partner.
{{smaller block|Go with my friend Moses, and represent Premium, and then, I’ll ''answer for'' it, you’ll see your nephew in all his glory.
{{right|''Sheridan'', School for Scandal, iii. 1.}}}}
'''4.''' To act or suffer in consequence of responsibility; meet the consequences: with ''for'', rarely absolutely.
{{smaller block|Let his neck ''answer for'' it, if there is any martial law.
{{right|''Shak.'', Hen. V., iv. 8.}}}}
{{smaller block|Every faculty which is a receiver of pleasure has an equal penalty put on its abuse. It is to ''answer for'' its moderation with its life.
{{right|''Emerson'', Compensation.}}}}
'''5.''' To meet, satisfy, or fulfil one’s wishes, expectations, or requirements; be of service: with ''for;'' absolutely, to serve the purpose; attain the end; suit; serve or do (well or ill, etc.).
{{smaller block|<poem>Long metre ''answers for'' a common song,
But common metre does not ''answer'' long.</poem>
{{right|''O. W. Holmes'', A Modest Request.}}}}
'''6.''' To conform, correspond; be similar, equivalent, proportionate, or correlative in character, quality, or condition: with ''to''.
{{smaller block|As in water face ''answereth to'' face, so the heart of man to man.
{{right|Prov. xxvii. 19.}}}}
{{smaller block|Sizar, a word still used in Cambridge, ''answers to'' a servitor in Oxford.
{{right|''Swift.''}}}}
{{smaller block|In thoughts which ''answer to'' my own. {{right|''Whittier'', Follen.}}}}
'''II.''' ''trans.'' '''1.''' To make answer to; speak or write in reply to; reply or respond to.
{{smaller block|<poem>So spake the apostate angel, though in pain; . . .
And him thus ''answer’d'' soon his bold compeer.</poem>
{{right|''Milton'', P. L., i. 125.}}}}
{{smaller block|In particular—(''a'') To reply to a charge or an accusation by; make a statement to, or in reply to, in defense or justification of one’s self with regard to a charge or an accusation.}}
<poem>I will . . .
Send him to ''answer'' thee, or any man,
For anything he shall be charg’d withal.</poem>
{{smaller block|{{right|''Shak.'', 1 Hen. IV., ii. 4.}}}}
{{smaller block|(''b'') To solve; find the result of; give an answer to, as to a question set for examination: as, he ''answered'' every question.}}

'''2.''' To say or offer in reply, or in reply to; utter, or enunciate to, by way of response.

{{smaller block|I will . . . watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall ''answer'' when I am reproved.{{right|Hab. ii. 1.}}}}
{{smaller block|That ye may have somewhat to ''answer'' them which glory in appearance.{{right|2 Cor. v. 12.}}}}

'''3.''' To reply or respond to in act; act or move in response to or in consequence of: either as a mere result, in obedience to or sympathy with, or as a hostile act in retaliation or reprisal against: as, to ''answer'' prayer; to ''answer'' a summons; to ''answer'' a signal, as a ring at the door: hence, to ''answer'' the bell, or the door; to ''answer'' the helm (said of a ship when she obeys her rudder).

{{smaller block|Blood hath bought blood, and blows have ''answer’d'' blows.{{right|''Shak.'', K. John, ii. 2.}}}}
{{smaller block|The woman had left us to ''answer'' the bell.{{right|''W. Collins'', Armadale, III. 205.}}}}

'''4†.''' To be responsible for; be accountable for.

<poem>''Answer'' my life my judgment,
Thy youngest daughter does not love thee least.</poem>
{{smaller block|{{right|''Shak.'', Lear, i. 1.}}}}

'''5.''' To act or suffer in consequence of responsibility for; meet the consequences of; atone for; make amends for; make satisfaction for.
{{smaller block|<poem>And do him right, that, ''answering'' one foul wrong,
Lives not to act another. {{right|''Shak.'', M. for M., ii. 2.}}</poem>
If it were so, it was a grievous fault,
And grievously hath Cæsar ''answer’d'' it [orig. ''answered for'' it].
{{right|''Shak.'', J. C., iii. 2.}}}}
'''6.''' To meet, satisfy, or fulfil one’s wishes, expectations, or requirements with regard to; satisfy (a claim); repay (an expense); serve (the purpose); accomplish (the end); serve; suit.
{{smaller block|<poem>This proud king; who studies, day and night,
To ''answer'' all the debt he owes unto you.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', 1 Hen. IV., i. 3.}}}}
{{smaller block|My returns will be sufficient to ''answer'' my expense and hazard. {{right|''Steele'', Spectator, No. 174.}}}}
{{smaller block|But, come, get to your pulpit, Mr. Auctioneer; here’s an old gouty chair of my father’s will ''answer'' the purpose.
{{right|''Sheridan'', School for Scandal, iv. 1.}}}}
'''7.''' To conform to; correspond to; be similar, equivalent, proportionate, or correlative to in quality, attributes, position, etc.
{{smaller block|<poem>Your mind’s pureness ''answers''
Your outward beauties.</poem>
{{right|''Massinger'', The Renegade, iv. 3.}}}}
{{smaller block|The windows ''answering'' each other, we could just discern the glowing horizon through them.
{{right|''W. Gilpin'', Tour to Lakes.}}}}
'''8.''' To meet or confront. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|Thou wert better in a grave, than to ''answer'' with thy uncovered body this extremity of the skies.
{{right|''Shak.'', Lear, iii. 4.}}}}

'''answerable''' (ȧn′sėr-a̤-bl), ''a.''   [< ''answer'' + ''-able.'']   '''1.''' Capable of being answered; admitting of a satisfactory reply.
{{smaller block|Unanswerable is a boastful word. His best reasons are ''answerable''; his worst are not worthy of being answered.
{{right|''Jeremy Collier'', Moral Subjects.}}}}
'''2.''' Liable to give an account or to be called to account; responsible; amenable: as, an agent is ''answerable'' to his principal.
{{smaller block|Will any man argue that . . . he cannot be justly punished, but is ''answerable'' only to God?
{{right|''Swift.''}}}}
{{smaller block|She’s to be ''answerable'' for its forthcoming.
{{right|''Goldsmith'', She Stoops to Conquer, iv.}}}}
'''3.''' Correspondent; similar; agreeing; in conformity; suitable; proportionate; correlative; equal. [Obsolescent.]
{{smaller block|It was but such a likeness as an imperfect glass doth give—''answerable'' enough in some features, but erring in others.
{{right|''Sir P. Sidney.''}}}}
{{smaller block|A faire dining-roome, and the rest of y<sup>e</sup> lodgings ''answerable'', with a pretty chappell.
{{right|''Evelyn'', Diary, Aug. 31, 1654.}}}}
{{smaller block|This revelation . . . was ''answerable'' to that of the apostle to the Thessalonians.
{{right|''Milton.''}}}}
{{smaller block|His Sentiments are every way ''answerable'' to his Character.
{{right|''Addison'', Spectator, No. 303.}}}}

'''answerableness''' (ȧn′sėr-a̤-bl-nes), ''n.'' '''1.''' Capability of being answered.—'''2.''' The quality of being answerable or responsible; liability to be called to account; responsibility.—'''3.''' The quality of being answerable or conformable; adaptability; agreement.

{{smaller block|The correspondency and ''answerableness'' which is between this bridegroom and his spouse.
{{right|''Harmar'', tr. of Beza, p. 196.}}}}

'''answerably''' (ȧn′sėr-a̤-bli), ''adv.'' In due proportion, correspondence, or conformity; proportionately; suitably.
{{smaller block|Continents have rivers ''answerably'' larger than islands.
{{right|''Brerewood.''}}}}

'''answerer''' (ȧn′sėr-ėr), ''n.'' One who answers; in school disputations, the respondent, that is, one who takes the initiative by propounding a thesis which he undertakes to maintain and defend against the objections of the opponents. See ''respondent.''
{{smaller block|The ''Answerer'' is of opinion, there is nothing to be done, no satisfaction to be had in matters of religion, without dispute; that is his only receipt, his nostrum for attaining a true belief.
{{right|''Dryden'', Def. of Duchess of York’s Paper.}}}}

'''answeringly''' (ȧn′sėr-ing-li), ''adv.'' So as to answer; correspondingly.

'''answer-jobber†''' (ȧn′sėr-job″ėr), ''n.'' One who makes a business of writing answers. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|What disgusts me from having anything to do with this race of ''answer-jobbers'', is, that they have no sort of conscience in their dealing.
{{right|''Swift'', Barrier Treaty.}}}}

'''answerless''' (ȧn′sėr-les), ''a.''   [< ''answer'' + ''-less.'']   '''1.''' Without an answer; having no answer to give.—'''2.''' Unanswered: as, ''answerless'' prayers. —'''3.''' Containing no sufficient or satisfactory answer; offering no substantial reply, while professing to do so.
{{smaller block|Here is an ''answerless'' answer, without confessing or denying either proposition.
{{right|''Abp. Bramhall'', II. 627.}}}} '''4.''' Incapable of being answered; unanswerable: as, an ''answerless'' question, argument, etc.

'''answerlessly''' (ȧn′sėr-les-li), ''adv.'' In an answerless manner; with an insufficient answer.
{{smaller block|Answered indeed; but, as he said, . . . ''answerlessly.''
{{right|''Bp. Hall'', Married Clergy.}}}}

'''ant<sup>1</sup>''' (ȧnt), ''n.''   [Early mod. E. ''ante'', ''ampte'', < ME. ''amte'', ''amete'', < AS. ''ǣmete'', ''ǣmette'' (also *''ēmete'', > ME. ''emete'', ''emette'', ''emet'', E. ''emmet'', q. v.) = OHG. ''āmeiza'', MHG. ''ameize'', G. ''ameise'' (MHG. also ''emeze'', G. ''emse''), ant. Of uncertain origin; perhaps < AS. ''ā-'', E. ''a-''<sup>1</sup> (also found accented in AS. ''ā-cumba'', E. ''oakum''), + *''mǣtan'' (in deriv. ''mettan'', (cut, engrave, hence) paint, depict; cf. ''metere'', a stone-cutter, and G. ''stein-metz'', a stone-cutter) = OHG. ''meizan'', MHG. ''meizen'', = Icel. ''meita'', cut. The lit. sense would then be ‘the cutter or biter off’; unless the term be taken passively, in a sense like that of Gr. ἔντομον or L. ''insectum'', insect, lit. ‘cut in.’ The G. form is commonly referred (through MHG. ''emeze'', G. ''emse'') to G. ''emsig'', MHG. ''emzic'', OHG. ''emizzig'', ''emazzig'', industrious, assiduous, which agrees formally, but not in sense, with AS. ''ǣmetig'', ''emtig'', E. ''empty'', q. v. See ''mire''<sup>2</sup> and ''pismire''.]   An emmet; a hymenopterous insect of the family ''Formicidæ'' and the Linnean genus ''Formica'', now divided into several genera. {{smaller|Ants live in communities, and the internal economy of their nest or hillock presents an extraordinary example of the results of combined industry. Each community comprises males with four wings, females much larger than the males and possessing wings during the pairing season only, and barren females, called neuters, workers, or nurses, destitute of wings.
